name: Rochelle Jordan
label: Empire
lede: Rochelle Jordan posts R&B covers on YouTube, gets ten DMs from a Virginia Beach producer, loses seven years to a bad deal, and comes back with a 17-track house album that Pitchfork ranks No. 25 for 2025.

eras.title: Ten DMs from Virginia Beach
eras.text: A girl raised near Toronto on her brother's gospel, house and jungle tapes posts R&B covers online. A producer who won't stop messaging her finds them. The partnership is still running.

years.h: Born in High Wycombe, raised in Wheatley, Ontario
years.p: Her Jamaican parents move the family to Wheatley when she is 4. She is diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at 2.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, her father was a musician, and frequent hospital stays marked her childhood. The FADER adds that she is the youngest of three, with two older brothers seven and ten years her senior.

Her brother Junior's tapes set her ears: gospel, house, drum and bass, jungle. She has named UK rave culture, absorbed on visits to family in London, as another root.

years.src: The FADER · Paste · RANGE · Wikipedia: Rochelle Jordan · NME
years.h: Ten DMs land in a row, all from a Virginia Beach producer
years.p: [[KLSH|3bf71d97-a5f8-4e74-bca4-fe52059f4c16]] finds her R&B covers on YouTube and keeps writing until she answers. He is still executive producer on everything she releases.
years.xp:
The FADER reports KLSH sent ten consecutive direct messages. Paste says they connected over a MySpace beat called "Neptune", and quotes her recalling her reaction: "What?!?! This is my producer". RANGE reports he flew her to Los Angeles for sessions. Paste dates her move to LA to age 19. Their first release together was the 2010 mixtape Alien Phase.

Wikipedia has her uploading covers at 16, inspired by Justin Bieber's YouTube start; NME puts her first singing videos at 19. The sources differ on the age.

eras.title: Namechecked, then blog-famous
eras.text: Three mixtapes in two years, a Drake mention, a Childish Gambino cut and a debut album made in a Los Angeles bedroom. The Aaliyah comparisons arrive before her sound has a name.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan at the mic, Los Angeles, January 2013
years.h: Drake says her name on "Club Paradise"
years.p: [[Drake|9fff2f8a-21e6-47de-a2b8-7f449929d43f]] mentions her on the 2011 mixtape the same year she puts out two of her own, Rojo and Origins.
years.xp: Paste reports she later worked out what the mention meant: her habit of stripping rap beats down to bare bones in R&B remixes, including a "Marvin's Room" remix Drake reportedly liked.

years.h: Pressure, mixtape number three, gets a trap-soul label
years.p: Now Toronto covers it in August 2012, styling the title "P R E S S U R E".
years.xp: Paste describes the project as trap soul.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan opening for Jessie Ware at The El Rey, Los Angeles, January 23, 2013
years.h: Childish Gambino puts her on "Telegraph Ave."
years.p: [[Childish Gambino|7fb57fba-a6ef-44c2-abab-2fa3bdee607e]] brings her in for a track on Because the Internet, the same year she is opening for Jessie Ware at The El Rey.
years.xp: NME lists the Gambino collaboration beside the Drake mention as the early sign that the blogs weren't her ceiling. The credit is NME's; no second source in the file confirms it.

years.h: Her debut, 1021, is named for her birthday
years.p: October 21. "Lowkey" and "Follow Me" come out of this period and stay her calling cards.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she recorded it in her Los Angeles bedroom. Vice ran a feature that November headlined "Rochelle Jordan is Making R&B That Brings the Whole World to Your Bedroom". In 2015, YouKnowIGotSoul interviewed her about the Toronto sound and the Aaliyah comparisons.

Paste dates "Follow Me" and "Lowkey" to 2014. "Lowkey" will be a TikTok hit a decade later.

eras.title: The wall
eras.text: The good reviews don't become a career. A contract she calls toxic, and her health, swallow almost seven years.

years.big: "I had to learn to not let anybody strangle or suffocate my career again."
q: I had to learn to not let anybody strangle or suffocate my career again.
years.src: Paste · Wikipedia: Play with the Changes · The Guardian
years.h: Seven years in a deal she calls toxic
years.p: After 1021 she signs what she later calls a "toxic" record deal. Wikipedia says the pressure and her health fed a near-seven-year silence.
years.xp:
Paste reports she spent years waiting on an A&R representative who never delivered, and that she describes the wall that built up around that relationship as something she had to take an ax to. She ended it near the end of the 2010s and went independent.

The Guardian ran the line above as the headline of its 2021 interview, per Wikipedia.

years.h: TOKiMONSTA's Young Art label signs her
years.p: [[TOKiMONSTA|96f6ec97-998c-4991-b836-7b71feb3ca6f]] gives her a home, and the silence after 1021 ends.

eras.title: Back on her own terms
eras.text: Seven years after her debut she returns with a club record about depression, longing and police brutality. Critics treat it as a comeback.

years.src: Wikipedia: Play with the Changes · Bandcamp Daily · The Culture Crypt
years.h: After seven years, Play with the Changes
years.p: Her second album, on Young Art, is built on UK garage, drum and bass, house and jungle. It sits at 86 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
KLSH is the main producer, with [[Machinedrum|d1785218-d8f4-4a83-a33d-8cf737eef918]] mixing and co-producing, plus [[Jimmy Edgar|fa263cb3-205f-4a7f-91e1-94e3df52abe8]], Alix Perez and Sepalcure. Farrah Fawx guests on "Broken Steel". Bandcamp Daily notes she recorded it in her bedroom, like her earlier records.

Wikipedia lists it on year-end lists at Exclaim!, Clash and PopMatters (No. 10), and on the Polaris Music Prize long list. A remix edition featured Kaytranada, Sango, KLSH and LSDXOXO, per The Culture Crypt.

eras.title: The old song came back first
eras.text: A decade-old track catches fire on TikTok, Empire signs her, and a 17-track house album lands on year-end lists.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan at Golden Plains, Victoria, Australia, March 2023
years.h: "Lowkey" blows up on TikTok a decade late
years.p: The 2014 song from 1021 takes off, and The Culture Crypt puts it near 30 million streams by 2024.
years.xp: NME dates the TikTok surge to 2024. The same year she appears on [[Kelela|045494aa-e913-4e62-bf4e-dcc276e0075a]]'s RAVE:N, The Remixes and [[Kaytranada|e56aee57-d90e-40cf-a70d-beb70f6f3c69]]'s TIMELESS, per The Culture Crypt.

years.p: The independent label takes her on, and president Tina Davis calls her the most important piece of its dance roster, per The FADER.
years.xp: The FADER quotes Davis on the pitch: "Her talent precedes her." The label's marketing, the piece says, put Jordan out front of the producers on the records rather than behind them.

yt: Doing It Too on Good Morning America
years.h: "Crave" opens a run of four singles
years.p: "Crave" goes out May 30, "TTW" on July 11, "Doing It Too" on August 8 and "Sweet Sensation" on September 12.
years.xp: "Doing It Too" got a television slot: Good Morning America.

years.src: Album of the Year · Metacritic · Beatportal · Paste · Wikipedia: Through the Wall · Pop Crave · NME
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and ranked it No. 25 of 2025. Metacritic has it at 90 from five critics.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Album of the Year list it as a September 26, 2025 release on Empire. Album of the Year records Pitchfork's 83 (Gio Santiago), calling it a sleek, perfectly executed club record. Metacritic's Line of Best Fit and AllMusic each gave 90, Consequence and Pitchfork 83.

KLSH is executive producer. Beatportal credits Kaytranada on "The Boy", Jimmy Edgar on "Bite the Bait" and [[DāM-FunK|6d6d607e-679a-4cdc-a7a0-35e2abe06619]] on "Sweet Sensation", with Byron the Aquarius, Hamdi and MPH also on the list. Paste has Initial Talk and Terry Hunter as well.

She told NME, of the stage persona behind the record: "It's time to let the dolls know that I know who I am - and I'm a muse."

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan at Fortune Sound Club, Vancouver, April 11, 2026
years.src: Album of the Year · Pop Crave · Wikipedia: Through the Wall · The FADER
years.h: The FADER puts it at No. 2, Pitchfork at No. 25
years.p: Album of the Year logs both, and Wikipedia adds CBC's best Canadian albums list at No. 3.
years.xp: Pop Crave posted Pitchfork's placement, with the 8.3 score, on December 5, 2025. The FADER followed with a March 2026 cover story on her slow burn.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan at The Opera House, Toronto, March 20, 2026
years.h: Sold-out fall dates turn into a world tour
years.p: North American dates in autumn 2025 sell out, then she adds Europe in February 2026 and North America in March and April.
years.xp: The fan-shot Philadelphia video is the full TLA set from March 24, 2026.

years.cap: Rochelle Jordan at Oya Festival, Oslo, August 13, 2026
years.h: The Polaris long list takes the album and "The Boy"
years.p: Through the Wall makes the 2026 Polaris Music Prize long list, and "The Boy" lands on the SOCAN Polaris Song Prize long list.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites Exclaim!'s June 11, 2026 long-list report and CBC Music's June 24 song-prize list.
